exposure: Poor pre-gestational pulmonary function (forced expiratory volume (FEV1) <= 50%)
cohort: The study included 149 women with cystic fibrosis without lung transplantation who had a first delivery reported to the French cystic fibrosis registry between 2000 and 2012.
finding: Poor pre-gestational pulmonary function in women with cystic fibrosis was associated with a higher rate of cesarean section and lower infant birthweight, but not with a greater decline in pulmonary function or BMI over the follow-up period.
mod_finding: The rate of cesarean section was significantly higher in women with FEV1 <= 50% (43.7%) compared to those with FEV1 > 50% (21.1%).
birth_weight: Range: 650-3860 g (median 2705 g for exposed group, 3044 g for unexposed group)
